mainTopic: Delayed betrothals and רבי יוחנן's 'leftover' idea, then the משנה on קידושין with money conditions and when they take effect
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's case of three men who each betroth the same woman 'from now and after' a set number of days. She needs a גט from the first and the last, but not from the middle one, whichever way the words are read. רבי יוחנן, reported by עולא and רבי אסי, holds that even a hundred such betrothals can take hold, because each one leaves a gap for the next, like a row of bricks. רב חנינא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא: a גט 'from today and after death' is doubtful, so she does חליצה but not יבום. רבא answers that death finishes what the גט left over, but אביי rejects this. אביי explains instead that under רבי יוחנן the ban on יבום is only a rabbinic decree, because the case looks like the valid גט 'from today if I die'. A new משנה then lists קידושין made on money conditions: giving, having, or showing 200 זוז. The גמרא brings the argument between רב הונא ('and he shall give') and רב יהודה ('when he gives') about when such a betrothal takes effect. It applies the same argument to a גט given on condition that she pays.

steps.title: The third man and אביי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A third man betroths her 'from now and after ten days.' אביי rules that she needs a גט from the first and the last man, but not from the middle one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another man came and said to her: 'You are betrothed to me from now and after ten days.' From the first and from the last she needs a גט. From the middle one she does not need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's case with a third man, then gives the ruling: she needs a גט from the first and last men, but not from the middle one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from now and after X days' are unclear in meaning. So she must be divorced from anyone who might really be her husband. The middle man can never be her husband, so she needs nothing from him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'from now and after' (the unclear wording at the center of the case)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The last' here means the man who said ten days. His betrothal is the first one to finish counting down, even though he spoke last.

phrases.english: And another came and said to her:
'You are hereby betrothed to me
from now and after ten days,'
from the first and from the last, she needs a bill of divorce;
from the middle one, she does not need a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She needs a גט from the first and last men, and none from the middle man.

steps.title: Either way, the middle man loses
steps.stepSummary: Whether the wording is a תנאי (condition) or a חזרה (retraction), the middle man's betrothal never takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if it is a condition, the first man's betrothal is valid and the others are not. If it is a retraction, the last man's betrothal is valid and the others are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for אביי's ruling with a 'מה נפשך' (either way you look at it) argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'from now' is the real meaning and 'after X days' is only a condition, the first man's betrothal already took effect, and nobody after him can betroth her. If 'after X days' takes back the 'from now,' each betrothal is delayed, and the ten-day man finishes first. In neither case does the middle man (twenty days) end up as her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: 'whichever way you want' (both options lead to the same result)
a condition: she is betrothed now, as long as the condition holds
a retraction: he took back 'from now' and delayed the betrothal
the first one / the last one

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if it is a condition,
the first man's is a betrothal,
those others' are not betrothals.
If it is a retraction,
the last man's is a betrothal,
those others' are not betrothals.
phrases.notes: Under this option, the first two men delayed longer (thirty and twenty days), so the ten-day man gets there first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under either reading of the wording, only the first or the last man can be the husband, never the middle one.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי: his conclusion seems so simple that it did not need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'מה נפשך' logic looks airtight. So what new thing is אביי teaching us? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it's obvious!' (a challenge asking what new point is being taught)

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for אביי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the logic is so clear, the statement teaches nothing new.

steps.title: We might have thought she needs a גט from everyone
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought the wording can mean either option for each man separately, so she would need a גט from all three. אביי teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this wording means a condition and also means a retraction, so she should need a גט from each and every one. So he teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing a mistaken idea that אביי's ruling rules out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought each man could have meant something different. For example, the first man retracted while the second set a condition, which would make the middle man the husband. אביי teaches that the doubt is about what the words themselves mean. So the same meaning applies to everyone who says them, and the middle man is never the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you might have said' (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The doubt in 'מעכשיו ולאחר' is about the meaning of the words themselves, not about each speaker's private intention. So one answer applies to all the men.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this wording means a condition
and means a retraction,
and she should need a bill of divorce from each and every one;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the new point (a mistaken idea that is ruled out)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each man's words could carry a different meaning, so she would need a גט from all three.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording has a single meaning (we just don't know which), so the middle man is never the husband.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a hundred can take hold
steps.stepSummary: עולא and רבי אסי both report that רבי יוחנן said even a hundred men can each take hold of her in this kind of betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even a hundred can take hold of her. And likewise רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even a hundred can take hold of her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רבי יוחנן holds that when betrothals are delayed like this, many men in a row can each catch hold of the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each delayed betrothal has not fully taken effect yet. That leaves room for another man to step in, then another, even up to a hundred. Two separate students report the same ruling, which makes it stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'take hold' (the betrothal takes effect on her)
and likewise (a second report of the same teaching)

phrases.english: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
Even a hundred take hold of her.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And likewise רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
Even a hundred take hold of her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to רבי יוחנן's view about many delayed betrothals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a hundred men's delayed betrothals can each take hold of her.

steps.title: Like a row of bricks with gaps
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא explains רבי יוחנן's reason: each man's betrothal leaves a gap for the next, like bricks in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא son of רב אמי said to רבי אסי: I will explain רבי יוחנן's reason to you. They made themselves like a row of bricks, where each one left space for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's 'even a hundred' with a picture: a row of bricks with spaces between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man's betrothal only finishes taking effect later. That waiting time is like a gap between bricks, and the next man's betrothal can fit into it. So each new man 'slots in' before the one before him is complete.
steps.whatToRemember: A delayed betrothal leaves an open window. According to רבי יוחנן, another betrothal can fit into that window, again and again.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רב משרשיא son of רב אמי said to רבי אסי:
I will explain to you the reason of רבי יוחנן:
they made themselves like a row of bricks,
where each and every one
left a space for his friend.
phrases.notes: He means the waiting time before each betrothal takes effect is the 'space' where the next man can come in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each delayed betrothal leaves a gap that the next betrothal can fill.

steps.title: רב חנינא quotes a ruling about a גט 'from today and after death'
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא: a גט 'from today and after death' is a doubtful גט, so the widow does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא challenges: If a man gives a גט 'from today and after death', it is a גט and not a גט. So if he dies, she does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רב חנינא quotes a ברייתא, and the next steps will show whom it causes a problem for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'from today and after death' is unclear. If 'from today' counts, she is divorced and forbidden to the יבם. If it does not, she is a widow who needs יבום or חליצה. Because of this doubt, she takes the safe path: חליצה, but no יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
A divorce and not a divorce, meaning a doubtful divorce
She does חליצה, the ceremony that releases her from יבום
She marries the יבם (her late husband's brother) through יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the doubt makes her free of everything. She still needs חליצה in case the גט did not work. She just cannot do יבום, in case the גט did work and she is forbidden to the brother.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina raises an objection:
"[This is your get] from today and after death" —
phrases.notes: This is a ברייתא. The husband means 'my death.'

phrases.english: it is a get and it is not a get,
and if he dies —
she does חליצה but does not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test the view of רבי יוחנן from steps 5-6, along with the views of רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוחנן that this kind of wording leaves a 'leftover'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא calls this גט doubtful. The clash with רבי יוחנן is spelled out in step 9.

steps.title: The ruling fits רב, and שמואל can explain it too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא fits רב well. שמואל can say it follows the רבנן, while he himself rules like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine for רב, since the ברייתא supports him. It is fine for שמואל too: whose view is this? It is the רבנן, and I rule like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears away the people who have no problem with this ברייתא. It is getting ready to aim the challenge at רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats this kind of wording as a doubt, so a doubtful גט is exactly what he would expect. שמואל reads the wording differently, as a condition. He says this ברייתא follows the רבנן, but he follows רבי, who disagrees with them. So neither of them is bothered.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works fine for, used before a 'but' (אלא)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav, it supports him,
according to Shmuel too [there is no problem]:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis,
and I say [my ruling] like Rabbi.
phrases.notes: Here שמואל is speaking about himself. 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא from step 7 causes no trouble for רב or שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: Narrowing the challenge down to רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'granted' (בשלמא) half of the challenge, which sets up the 'but' that comes next.

steps.title: But for רבי יוחנן, יבום should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, this wording leaves a 'leftover'. A גט that leaves anything over is worth nothing, so the woman should be allowed יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוחנן, who said this wording leaves a leftover: any גט that leaves something over in her is nothing at all. So the יבם should be able to do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge. The ברייתא seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said this kind of wording leaves a 'gap' or 'leftover'. When the wording is used in a גט, the marriage is not fully cut today. There is a rule that a גט must cut the marriage completely, or it is not a גט at all. So the גט should be totally void, she is a plain widow, and יבום should be allowed. Yet the ברייתא forbids יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover, a part that is held back
It is nothing at all, completely invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a basic rule of גיטין: a גט must cut the bond completely. That rule is what makes רבי יוחנן's 'leftover' idea a problem here.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said it is a leftover,
phrases.notes: This points back to steps 5-6, where each betrothal leaves a gap for the next one.

phrases.english: any get that leaves something over in her
is nothing at all.
He should surely be able to do יבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר שִׁיּוּרָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'granted... but' challenge by aiming it at רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that this wording leaves a 'leftover'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wording leaves a leftover, the גט fails the rule that a גט must cut the marriage completely. Then it is void, and יבום should be allowed. That goes against the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: death finishes what the get left over
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a גט and death both release a woman. Whatever the גט left over, death completes, so the release is full.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A גט releases her, and death releases her. Whatever the גט left over, death finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי יוחנן. He explains why this גט is not totally void, even though it leaves something over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a leftover ruins a גט applies when nothing fills in the gap. Here the part of the marriage the גט left for 'after death' is ended by the death itself. Together the two make a full release, so the גט has real force, and יבום is not allowed.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A get is to release [her], and death is to release [her],
what the get left over, death completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא גֵּט לְהוֹצִיא וּמִיתָה לְהוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joining two causes: the גט and the death together make one full release.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט that leaves something over is worthless, so she is a plain widow who may do יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death fills in the leftover, so the release is complete and יבום is not allowed.

steps.title: אביי: a get and death pull in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's answer. A גט takes a woman out of the יבם's reach, but death brings her into it, so they cannot complete each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is it comparable? A גט takes her out of the יבם's domain, but death brings her into the יבם's domain!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer. He argues that a גט and death cannot be added together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a גט and death end the marriage to the husband, but they have opposite results for the brother. A divorced woman is forbidden to the יבם. A widow without children is tied to the יבם. So death cannot 'finish' a release from the יבם that the גט was supposed to give.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא joins the גט and the death together, since both end the marriage. אביי says they cannot join, since a גט pushes her away from the יבם while death ties her to him.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Is it comparable?
A get takes her out of the yavam's domain,
death brings her into the yavam's domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer רבא gave in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's idea that death completes what the גט left over
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גט and death have opposite effects regarding the יבם, so they cannot combine into one complete release.

steps.title: אביי's new answer: the rule is only a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that under רבי יוחנן the גט is truly worthless, so by Torah law she is a widow tied to the יבם and could even do יבום. The חכמים forbade יבום only as a decree, because the case looks like the valid גט 'from today if I die'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: What is the reason there? It is a decree because of a גט given 'from today if I die', which is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops רבא's answer and gives his own way to explain the ברייתא according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the woman can't do יבום if the גט is worthless. אביי answers that by Torah law she could. The חכמים forbade it only because people might confuse this case with 'from today if I die', which really is a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים
'From today if I die', a גט that really works if he dies

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole picture. The ברייתא's rule is no longer seen as a Torah-level doubt. It is a rabbinic safeguard, and that sets up the rest of the back-and-forth.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
There, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא's case of 'from today and after death', where she does חליצה but not יבום.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of 'from today if I die'
which is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new answer to the challenge in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the ruling as a rabbinic decree based on a look-alike case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling of חליצה without יבום must mean the גט has some real effect
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט is worthless by Torah law. The חכמים forbade יבום only so people would not confuse it with a valid 'from today if I die' גט

steps.title: Why not make the decree go both ways?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים don't also require חליצה in the valid case of 'from today if I die', so the two cases look the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us decree that with 'from today if I die' she must do חליצה, because of 'from today and after death'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי: if the two cases can be confused, why not make the decree work in the other direction too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the valid case, 'from today if I die', the woman is fully divorced and needs no חליצה at all. The גמרא asks why the חכמים don't add חליצה there too, so it matches the worthless case.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the worry about (a look-alike case)

phrases.english: But let us decree that with 'from today if I die' she must do chalitza,
because of 'from today and after death'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's decree from step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the חכמים decreed because the two cases look alike
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two cases are easily confused, the decree should also require חליצה in the valid case

steps.title: חליצה there would make people think יבום is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Requiring חליצה in the valid case would lead people to think יבום is also possible. Yet she is truly divorced and forbidden to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she does חליצה, people will say she can also do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים would not add חליצה in the valid 'from today if I die' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a woman who can do חליצה could also do יבום instead. In the valid case she is a real divorcée, and real יבום with her would be forbidden. Making her do חליצה could fool people into allowing that forbidden יבום.

phrases.english: If you say she does chalitza,
[people will think] she can also do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra decree would cause harm
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Adding חליצה to the valid case is just extra caution
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding חליצה would mislead people into allowing a truly forbidden יבום

steps.title: The same problem exists in the original case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the same worry applies to 'from today and after death'. There she does חליצה, so people may think יבום is allowed there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, if you say she does חליצה, people will think she can do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer back on the ברייתא's own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the woman does חליצה in the 'from today and after death' case. By the logic of step 14, people would then wrongly assume יבום is allowed there too. So why is חליצה required there?

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא's case, 'from today and after death'.

phrases.english: if you say she does chalitza,
[people will think] she can do yibum!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי אִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר חוֹלֶצֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 14 to challenge the ברייתא's requirement of חליצה
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of חליצה in the 'from today and after death' case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חליצה leads people to think יבום is allowed, the same danger exists in the ברייתא's case

steps.title: No harm: the ban there is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: In the 'from today and after death' case, even if someone did do יבום, nothing truly forbidden happens. The ban is only a rabbinic worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that. It is only a rabbinic concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the mistake would not matter in this case, because the woman is not truly divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן, the 'from today and after death' גט is worthless by Torah law. If people mistakenly allowed יבום there, no real sin would happen. In the valid 'from today if I die' case, the same mistake would lead to a real sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A worry of the חכמים, not a Torah prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, under רבי יוחנן the 'from today and after death' גט is worthless by Torah law. The rule of חליצה without יבום is only a rabbinic decree. The decree is not added to the valid 'from today if I die' case, because there a mistaken יבום would be a real sin.

phrases.english: Let her do yibum, and there is nothing wrong with that;
it is only a concern of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes אביי's line of reasoning
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a Torah-level danger from a rabbinic-level one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases carry the same risk of a mistaken יבום
steps.terutzMaskana: A mistaken יבום in the worthless-גט case breaks only a rabbinic rule. In the valid-גט case it would be a Torah sin, so only there is the risk avoided.

steps.title: Betrothal on condition of giving two hundred זוז
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a man betroths a woman 'on condition that I give you 200 זוז'. She is betrothed, and he must give the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me on condition that I give you 200 זוז', she is betrothed, and he must give.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about קידושין given with a condition of paying money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition does not undo the קידושין. She is betrothed, and the man must still pay the 200 זוז he promised.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says to a woman:
'You are hereby betrothed to me

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶתֵּן לִךְ מָאתַיִם זוּז״
phrases.english: on condition that I give you two hundred zuz'
she is betrothed,
and he must give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶתֵּן לִךְ מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion about a גט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין on condition of a future payment works, and the man must pay

steps.title: Betrothal on condition of paying within thirty days
steps.stepSummary: If the condition includes a deadline of thirty days, she is betrothed only if he pays within that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'on condition that I give you from now until thirty days', and he gave within thirty days, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case, where the condition has a time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the deadline is part of the condition. If he pays within thirty days, the condition is met and the קידושין stands. If he misses the deadline, the קידושין fails completely.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. With no deadline, she is betrothed and he simply owes the money. With a deadline, missing it cancels the קידושין.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I give you
from now until thirty days':
if he gave it to her within thirty [days],
she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶתֵּן לִךְ מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the משנה: a condition with a time limit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the condition sets a deadline, the קידושין works only if the payment is made in time

steps.title: Condition: 'that I have 200 זוז'
steps.stepSummary: If he betroths her on condition that he has 200 זוז, she is betrothed only if he really has that money.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On condition that I have 200 זוז': she is betrothed, if he has it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of money conditions. Here the man says he has 200 זוז, and the betrothal depends on whether that is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier cases, he doesn't have to give anything. It only matters whether the money truly exists in his possession. If he has it, the קידושין work. If he doesn't, they don't.

keyTerms.meaning: That I have (the condition is about something already true now)
If he has it (the betrothal depends on whether he really owns the money)

phrases.english: 'On condition that I have two hundred zuz' –
she is betrothed, if he has it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the same משנה's list of money conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition about owning money is fulfilled only if he truly has the money.

steps.title: Condition: 'that I show you 200 זוז'
steps.stepSummary: If he betroths her on condition that he will show her 200 זוז, he must show her his own money. Showing money from a money-changer's table does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On condition that I show you 200 זוז': she is betrothed, and he must show it to her. If he showed her money on the table, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another money condition: showing the money. It adds a limit: showing money that isn't really his doesn't fulfill the condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Show you 200 זוז' is understood to mean 'show you 200 זוז that are mine'. A money-changer showing coins from his business table is showing other people's money. So the condition is not met and there are no קידושין.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I show you two hundred zuz' –
she is betrothed, and he must show it to her.
And if he showed it on the table –
phrases.notes: This means a money-changer's table. The coins there belong to other people, not to him.

phrases.english: she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Showing money fulfills the condition only if it is his own money; table money does not count.
steps.whatToRemember: Every money condition in this משנה is read the way people normally mean it: give, have, or show money that is really his.

steps.title: Two readings of 'he must give'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports an argument about the wording of the first case of the משנה: רב הונא says 'and he shall give', and רב יהודה says 'when he gives'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא says 'and he shall give'. רב יהודה says 'when he gives'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by going back to the משנה's case of 'on condition that I give you 200 זוז' and quoting two versions of it. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions sound almost the same, but they point to different timing. 'And he shall give' sounds like she is already betrothed and he still owes the money. 'When he gives' sounds like the betrothal waits for the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an argument between אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: Both agree that if he never pays, she is not betrothed. They argue only about WHEN the betrothal takes hold.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav Huna says: 'And he shall give.'
phrases.notes: This is the ending of the משנה's case 'on condition that I give you 200 זוז' from step 17.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says: 'When he gives.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by returning to the first case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא reads 'and he shall give'; רב יהודה reads 'when he gives'.

steps.title: What each reading means
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: it is a condition, so she is betrothed now and he just fulfills it later. רב יהודה: the betrothal happens only once he pays, and right now there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says 'and he shall give': it is a condition, and he goes on to fulfill it. רב יהודה says 'when he gives': once he gives, there is betrothal, but right now there is no betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what lies behind each version of the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, once he pays, the קידושין count from the moment he first spoke. For רב יהודה, the קידושין begin only at the moment of payment. Until then she is not betrothed at all.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says 'and he shall give':
it is a condition,
he goes on and fulfills the condition.
phrases.notes: So she is betrothed already. Paying just completes the condition, and the betrothal counts from when he spoke.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says 'when he gives':
when he gives, it will be a betrothal,
but now, at any rate, it is not a betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: וְהוּא יִתֵּן תְּנָאָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two readings quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: betrothal now, counted from his words once he pays. רב יהודה: betrothal only from the moment of payment.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the two views would actually lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. In the end both need him to pay, so when would it matter? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he pays, she ends up betrothed under both views. If he doesn't pay, she is not betrothed under both views. So the גמרא wants a case where the timing itself makes a difference.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the argument in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רב הונא and רב יהודה would rule differently.

steps.title: Another man betroths her in between
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up if a second man betroths her before the first man pays. For רב הונא the second betrothal fails. For רב יהודה it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is where she reached out her hand and accepted betrothal from another man. According to רב הונא it is not a betrothal. According to רב יהודה it is a betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case: a second man betroths her while she is waiting for the first man's payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, once the first man pays, she counts as betrothed to him from the start, so she was never free for the second man. For רב יהודה, she was still single when the second man betrothed her, so his קידושין take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: She stretched out her hand (to accept)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: a conditional betrothal counts from the first moment, so a second man in between gets nothing. רב יהודה: it starts only at payment, so the second man's betrothal works.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where she stretched out her hand and accepted betrothal from another man.
phrases.notes: This happens after the first man spoke but before he paid.

phrases.english: According to Rav Huna, it is not a betrothal,
according to Rav Yehuda, it is a betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case where a second man betroths her before the first man pays: invalid for רב הונא, valid for רב יהודה.

steps.title: The same case with a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a parallel משנה about divorce: a גט given on condition that she pays 200 זוז. She is divorced, and she must give the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned about divorce in the same way: one who says to a woman, 'This is your גט on condition that you give me 200 זוז', she is divorced, and she shall give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a matching משנה from the laws of divorce. This sets up the same argument there in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the roles are switched: the woman has to pay, and the money is the condition for the גט. The wording 'and she shall give' raises the same timing question as in קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned (in a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי גִיטִּין כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא:
phrases.english: And we also learned concerning divorce documents a case like this:
One who says to a woman: 'This is your divorce document

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״ –
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz' –
she is divorced, and she shall give.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי גִיטִּין כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קידושין to a parallel משנה about a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given on condition that she pays 200 זוז works, and she must pay.

steps.title: The same argument about the גט
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב יהודה argue the same way about the גט. For רב הונא it is a condition she fulfills later. For רב יהודה the גט works only once she pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא says 'and she shall give'. רב יהודה says 'when she gives'. רב הונא says 'and she shall give': it is a condition, and she goes on to fulfill it. רב יהודה says 'when she gives': only when she gives it to him is it a גט, but right now it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two אמוראים keep their same positions in the divorce case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, once she pays, the divorce counts from when he handed her the גט. For רב יהודה, she is still married until she pays. Both use the same reasoning they used for קידושין.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא and רב יהודה argue the same way in both קידושין and גט: does a condition about payment take effect from the start (רב הונא) or only once payment is made (רב יהודה)?

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna says: 'And she shall give.'
Rav Yehuda says: 'When she gives.'
Rav Huna says 'and she shall give':
it is a condition, and she goes on and fulfills the condition.
Rav Yehuda says 'when she gives':

phrases.aramaic: לְכִי יָהֲבָה לֵיהּ הוּא דְּהָוֵי גֵּט,
phrases.english: only when she gives it to him is it a divorce document,
but now, at any rate, it is not a divorce document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: וְהִיא תִּתֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument of steps 21-22 to the גט case of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the גט works now, and she fulfills the condition later. רב יהודה: the גט takes effect only once she pays.
